body_md: Futures cancel on **drop**: `select!` loser is dropped mid-await. Make code cancellation-safe — no half-written state. Use guards or transactions that roll back.
hook: Dropping a future cancels it mid-sentence — is your code ready?
output: // select!: the loser is dropped mid-await — cancelled, destructors run

quiz.explain: Dropping future stops polls; destructors run cleanup.
quiz.q: What happens when a future is dropped?

takeaway: Design async ops to tolerate mid-point cancellation.
trap: Assuming select loser completes; shared state left half-updated.

body_md: `CancellationToken` (tokio-util) coordinates shutdown: `child_token.cancelled().await`. Clone per task, cancel parent to signal all. Cleaner than AtomicBool flags.
hook: Shut down 100 tasks with one call — CancellationToken.
output: // compiles with tokio-util: one cancel() wakes every cloned token

quiz.explain: Token broadcasts cancel to all child clones.
quiz.q: How do you signal shutdown to many tasks?

trap: Dropping token without cancel leaves tasks hanging.

body_md: **Backpressure** stops fast producers overwhelming slow consumers: bounded channels (`channel(16)`), `send().await` waits when full. Unbounded queues OOM under load.
code:
// let (tx, mut rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<T>(16);
// tx.send(item).await.unwrap(); // waits if full
hook: Unbounded channels are memory bombs — bounded ones push back.
output: // send().await waits when the 16-slot buffer is full (backpressure)

quiz.explain: Bounded send waits when buffer full, throttling producer.
quiz.q: How do bounded channels create backpressure?

takeaway: Bound channels to propagate pressure upstream.
trap: Unbounded_channel in hot path grows until OOM.

body_md: `tokio::sync::Semaphore` caps concurrent work: acquire permit per request. `Semaphore::new(32)` for DB pool. Permit guard releases on drop automatically.
hook: 32 slots, 1000 requests — Semaphore queues the rest fairly.
output: // compiles with tokio: at most 32 holders; permit guard releases on drop

quiz.explain: Acquire waits for free permit; drop releases.
quiz.q: How do you cap concurrent DB queries?

takeaway: Gate scarce resources with semaphore permits.
trap: Leaking permit guard (mem::forget) starves pool permanently.

body_md: `tokio::sync::RwLock` for read-heavy shared config. Many readers, one writer. Never hold across `.await` that needs write — yields while holding can deadlock.
code:
// let cfg = tokio::sync::RwLock::new(conf);
// { let r = cfg.read().await; use_cfg(&r); }
hook: 1000 readers, 1 writer — RwLock scales where Mutex stalls.
output: // compiles with tokio: many readers or one writer; never hold across await

quiz.explain: RwLock allows concurrent reads, exclusive writes.

body_md: Stream control: `buffered(n)` runs n futures concurrently, `buffer_unordered` finishes out-of-order, `throttle` rate-limits. From `futures::StreamExt` or `tokio-stream`.
hook: Fetch 100 URLs 10 at a time — one combinator does it.
output: // compiles with futures: 10 fetches concurrently, results in order

quiz.explain: buffered polls up to n futures at once.
quiz.q: How do you limit concurrent stream items?

takeaway: Shape stream concurrency with buffered combinators.
trap: Unbounded concurrency via buffer_unordered(10000) exhausts sockets.

body_md: Timeouts with `tokio::time::timeout(dur, fut).await`: Ok on success, Err on expiry. Always bound external calls. Retry with backoff via `tokio-retry` or loop + sleep.
code:
// let r = tokio::time::timeout(dur, fetch()).await;
// match r { Ok(v) => v, Err(_) => fallback() }
hook: Never await the network forever — wrap it in a timeout.
output: // Ok(value) on success, Err(Elapsed) on expiry → fallback()

quiz.explain: timeout returns Err if deadline passes first.
quiz.q: What does tokio timeout return on expiry?

takeaway: Bound every external await with timeout.
trap: Retrying without backoff hammers failing service; add jitter.

body_md: Spawn CPU work with `rayon` inside `spawn_blocking`, or `tokio::task::JoinSet` for dynamic tasks. `JoinSet::join_next` processes as each completes.
hook: Unknown number of tasks? JoinSet collects them as they finish.
output: // compiles with tokio: join_next() yields each result as it finishes

quiz.explain: JoinSet tracks dynamic tasks and joins incrementally.
quiz.q: How do you manage dynamic task counts?

trap: Spawning unbounded tasks exhausts memory; cap with semaphore.

body_md: Graceful shutdown: listen `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()`, then `token.cancel()`, `join_all` with deadline. Drain channels before exit to avoid data loss.
hook: Ctrl-C should drain, not destroy — graceful shutdown pattern.
output: // ctrl_c → cancel → drain with deadline; Ok(()) on clean shutdown

quiz.explain: Signal triggers cancel, tasks finish work then exit.

trap: Exiting without draining drops queued channel items.

body_md: `tokio::sync::watch` broadcasts latest config: sender `send(new)`, receivers `changed().await` then `borrow()`. Slow receivers skip to newest — no lag queue.
hook: Push config to 500 tasks instantly — watch keeps only the latest.
output: // send(new_cfg) wakes all watchers; slow ones skip to the latest

quiz.explain: watch holds one latest value; receivers observe changes.

trap: Broadcast for config replays stale backlog; watch coalesces.

body_md: Split borrows across await: compute owned data first, drop guards, then await. `MutexGuard` is not Send in std — holding across await blocks executor.
code:
// { let v = cache.lock().unwrap().clone(); }
// fetch(&v).await; // lock released before await
hook: Holding a lock across await freezes your async runtime.
output: // compiles: guard cloned-and-dropped before await — no lock held

quiz.explain: Clone needed data, drop guard, then await.
quiz.q: How do you use Mutex data across await?

takeaway: Never hold sync locks across await points.
trap: std MutexGuard across await fails Send check or deadlocks.

body_md: Tune runtime: `#[tokio::main(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]` for servers, `current_thread` for CLIs. Set `max_blocking_threads` for spawn_blocking pool.
hook: Default Tokio settings waste your server — tune the runtime.
output: // compiles with tokio: multi-thread runtime, 4 workers

quiz.q: Which Tokio flavor for high-throughput servers?

takeaway: Match runtime flavor to workload shape.
trap: current_thread with blocking work stalls everything.
